title: fix(backup): avoid false owner conflicts for duplicate registry paths
body:
Closes #153970. Thanks @RJAILLC for the report and reproduction details.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `backup create --verify` refusing duplicate registrations of one agent database and prevents registered hardlink aliases from losing committed WAL-only rows in the archive.

## User Impact

Verified backups preserve committed database rows regardless of alias pathname order, including with `--no-include-workspace`. Genuine two-owner conflicts and unsafe or changing journal ownership still refuse publication with a recorded reason. No new options, schema changes, or live registry rewrites are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace enclosing the state directory succeeds on its own. The original refusal reproduces when the captured registry carries two spellings of one agent database path, such as `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` and `agents/main/agent/./openclaw-agent.sqlite`, or a physical alias. The report did not include the reporter's registry rows, so its exact historical spelling is unknown. `sealBackupResourceInventory` deduplicates physical ownership while preserving archive alias names and rejecting different registered owners. The dry-run `skipped: covered` entries suppress duplicate top-level assets; discovery already deduplicates state/agent traversal.

ClawSweeper's P1 identified a data-loss hole in that first repair: the first registered hardlink pathname supplied every alias snapshot, and canonical sources bypassed WAL-aware grouping. An earlier-sorting alias without the owner's WAL could therefore omit committed rows. All sources now use the existing `planBackupSqliteSourceGroups` owner to select the journal-owning source independently of pathname order. Canonical validation, sanitization, cold-archive anchors, and final registration identity checks remain intact. The initial global group and private image remain authoritative for both the captured registry and later global aliases.

A separate-process alias writer can checkpoint and truncate its WAL between journal checks while a primary reader is pinned. The shared grouping owner now also checks the existing main-file mutation fingerprint (device/inode, size, and birth/change/modification timestamps) for multi-path groups, including cached-image copies. This refuses the transient checkpoint race without opening raw file descriptors that could release SQLite locks. Ordinary WAL appends remain valid.

Production interdiff versus `a12c801c4683eb8cf580d046108ba2f9cfa42944`: **+48 net LOC (+107/-59)**; tests **+183 (+188/-5)**; docs **+2 (+5/-3)**. The original duplicate-registration repair was +34 production LOC. The additional growth covers shared source planning, initial global-group ownership, and the checkpoint-race guard; the canonical bypass and separate alias snapshot path were removed.

## Evidence

- **Pre-fix reproduction:** duplicate-registry enclosing-home fixtures failed with the reported refusal in both workspace modes; enclosure alone succeeded. The WAL follow-up regressions failed before the source-selection repair, and the separate-process checkpoint case failed before the mutation-fingerprint guard.
- **39 focused tests passed** across five files on the published repair. Restored committed WAL-only rows survive alias-first and canonical-first order for agent and global databases. Competing WALs and rollback-journal ambiguity refuse with a recorded failure and no archive publication. A single nonempty WAL with no other alias WAL is the unambiguous supported case.
- **20/20 checkpoint-race repeatability runs passed**, with individual case time 0.429–2.511 seconds. The regression uses the existing `backupNodeSqliteDatabase` owner; no timeout increase or retry was added.
- **P1 autoreview: scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `git diff --check` passed locally.
- **CI attached** to `100f7e24cbfa9c77682053411deb544a049aed82`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35548393564). CI was running when this evidence was recorded; the other attached checks had passed.
- **Testbox cost, exact published source:** all 15 cases passed on Linux x86_64 / Node v24.19.0 (4 CPUs reported). Registered hardlinks: **22.719 s command wall / 7.509 s summed cases**, 7/7 passed. Ownership: **20.045 s command wall / 8.027 s summed cases**, 8/8 passed. Each file separately used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` with verbose + JSON reporters. Source-worker preparation took 7.633 s and 7.341 s respectively; wall includes that setup. [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35549975370), lease `tbx_01m30r5vdzt56wjg4me3c9w7h6`, provider `blacksmith-testbox`; source receipt and four relevant source hashes matched `100f7e24cbfa9c77682053411deb544a049aed82`. The remote command reported exit 0; portal synchronization subsequently emitted a deadline warning, after the complete timing reports were captured.
- **Cost disposition:** the saturated Mac's 239.477 s / 251.017 s summed case times and 59.217 s / 50.813 s maxima did not reproduce on Testbox. Neither file exceeded 120 s wall, and no case approached 30 s. No fixture consolidation or assertion changes were made. The retained tests exercise real SQLite WAL/hardlink behavior through create, verify, restore, and recorded refusal, which cannot be established by mocking those boundaries.
- **Earlier isolated CLI proof of duplicate registrations:** `backup create --verify` succeeded, the archive restored into a second isolated tree, and read-only Doctor passed. Global, agent, and quarantine integrity checks returned `ok`; the synthetic row and both registry spellings survived. This transcript predates the WAL follow-up; it is not a new CLI run at the current head. No operator state or Gateway was used.

<details>
<summary>Testbox top three cases per file</summary>

| File | Case | Seconds |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Registered hardlinks | Agent one-WAL restore, `a-alias.sqlite` (alias first) | 1.302 |
| Registered hardlinks | Global one-WAL restore, `a-alias.sqlite` (alias first) | 1.168 |
| Registered hardlinks | Global one-WAL restore, `z-alias.sqlite` (canonical first) | 1.167 |
| Ownership | Enclosing workspace, dot spelling, workspace included | 1.347 |
| Ownership | Agent registered immediately before root capture, registry restored | 1.292 |

```text
registered-hardlinks: 7 passed, 0 failed; wall=22.719 s; summed cases=7.509 s
ownership:           8 passed, 0 failed; wall=20.045 s; summed cases=8.027 s
```

Each file ran once in its own command. Local source-transfer preparation and provider setup are excluded from their measured command wall times. The earlier Mac figures are summed case times, not command wall times.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Sanitized command transcript and restored-state checks</summary>

Paths below are fixture placeholders; build chatter is omitted.

```text
# OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH select the source fixture.
$ pnpm openclaw backup create --verify --output <fixture>/backup.tar.gz --json
{"verified":true,"includeWorkspace":true,"onlyConfig":false,"skippedVolatileCount":0}
# The home workspace is the sole top-level asset. State and agent roots are covered.

$ pnpm openclaw backup restore <fixture>/backup.tar.gz --target <fixture>/restored --json
{"ok":true,"assetCount":1,"entryCount":12,"symlinkCount":0,"targetPath":"<fixture>/restored"}
# Standard restore warnings describe state rollback, channel relinking and plugin rebuilding.

# Select the extracted home/.openclaw using OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
# and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH. Re-anchor the copied config's absolute workspace
# to the extracted home and give that copied config mode 0600. No database edits.
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/agent-database-admission --only core/doctor/state-integrity --json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"checksRun":2,"checksSkipped":63,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/state-integrity","severity":"warning","message":"State directory permissions are too open. Recommend chmod 700."}]}

# The extracted state directory was 0755; prepare the isolated activation directory.
$ chmod 700 <restored-state>
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/agent-database-admission --only core/doctor/state-integrity --json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":2,"checksSkipped":63,"findings":[]}
# exit 0; no Doctor repair flags used.

# Independent immutable, read-only SQLite checks:
state/openclaw.sqlite: integrity_check=ok, role=global
agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: integrity_check=ok, role=agent, agent_id=main
state/openclaw-quarantine.sqlite: integrity_check=ok
proof_records: [["owner-alias-proof"]]
agent_databases:
  main | agents/main/agent/./openclaw-agent.sqlite
  main | agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
# Global and agent SHA-256 values were unchanged across both Doctor runs.
# Quarantine SHA-256 was unchanged across the final Doctor run.
```

`backup restore --dry-run` is not a supported option; the approved proof uses actual isolated restoration and read-only Doctor instead. The first restore attempt encountered the artifact lock retained by the previously stopped local checker. Its owner and recorded child were verified stopped, no build held the worktree artifacts, and only that task-owned lock residue was removed before the successful restore.

Focused test command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts -t 'backup SQLite ownership|canonical SQLite symlink retargets|sanitizes every in-state|agent SQLite symlink|canonical agent'
```

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       12 passed | 127 not selected (139)
```

</details>

## Review dispositions

Both ClawSweeper Rank-up moves are **applied**:

- **Preserve the journal-owning source when sharing registered-hardlink snapshots:** all alias sets use the existing WAL-aware source-group owner; canonical validation and sanitization are preserved.
- **Verify restored committed WAL-only rows in both pathname orders and retain refusal for ambiguous journal ownership:** agent/global restore cases cover both orders, and ambiguous journal states record a failure and publish no archive.

The additional autoreview checkpoint-race finding is also applied through the shared main-file fingerprint guard. The data-loss repair is published for a new lead-review round. No merge has been performed.
